html:
The Mytilenean revolt was a rising of Mytilene, the main city of the island of Lesbos, against Athens in 428 to 427 BCE, during the Peloponnesian War.

Mytilene was one of the few allies in the Delian League that still had its own fleet. It planned to break away with help from Sparta, but Athens found out and laid siege to the city. Spartan help came too late, and Mytilene surrendered in 427 BCE.

What happened next is one of the most famous scenes in Thucydides. Urged on by Cleon, the Athenian Assembly voted to kill all the men of Mytilene and sell the women and children as slaves, and a ship sailed with the order. The next day many citizens regretted the vote. In a second debate a speaker named Diodotus argued that mercy served Athens better, and the Assembly changed its mind. A second ship rowed day and night and arrived just as the first order was being read.

The city was spared, though more than a thousand leaders of the revolt were executed and Athenian settlers took over its land. Eleven years later, at Melos, Athens did not relent.
sum: The Mytilenean revolt was a rising of Mytilene, the main city of the island of Lesbos, against Athens in 428 to 427 BCE, during the Peloponnesian War.
